summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted due to increased redness, warmth, and swelling in her right knee, following a recent fall that caused a suprapatellar effusion. She was diagnosed with right knee cellulitis and treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral Bactrim and Keflex. Her potassium was repleted from 2.7 to 3.8 mEq/L, and her home dose was increased. She remained afebrile, ambulated without difficulty, and showed clinical improvement. Orthopedics did not recommend drainage or surgery. Due to recurrent falls and a history of cervical spine fracture, she was advised to use a walker and receive home physical therapy. She was discharged home with services, cleared for upcoming travel, and given follow-up appointments with her PCP, rheumatology, and wound clinic.
